chunks: Hammad, from Hareyz, from Zurara and Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

We said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'These winds and darknesses that occur, should one pray for them?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Every fear of the sky, from darkness, or wind, or terror, so pray for it the prayer of the eclipse, until it settles.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying for strong winds and darkness?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) expands the scope of the eclipse prayer (Salat al-Kusuf) to include any celestial or atmospheric phenomenon—such as strong winds, darkness, or general terror (faza')—that induces fear in the heart, treating them ritually equivalent to solar or lunar eclipses. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly understanding that the underlying cause for this prayer is the manifestation of divine power through natural signs that stir awe, rather than the specific astronomical event itself. It underscores the practical application of worship as a response to both cosmic and terrestrial disturbances.
